input.question: How do the same programs run on different operating systems?
input.ground_truth: There are development languages that are cross platform. This is one way this can be accomplished. The same code base will run in various environments (Linux/BSD/Windows) and then OS specific code can be ran inside the software that is called based on what environment the code detects. Also, a second way would be runtime emulation such as WINE, but I don't think that is what you are referring to

Okay! Imagine you have a toy car. You can play with your toy car on the floor at home (that’s like one operating system, like Windows), or you can take it to the park (that’s like another operating system, like Mac or Linux).

Now, imagine you have a set of instructions for your toy car, like "go forward," "turn left," and "beep beep." These instructions are like a program.

Even though the floor at home and the grass in the park are different, if your toy car understands the same instructions ("go forward," etc.), it can move and make sounds no matter where you are playing.

So, computer programs are like those instructions. If the program is written in a way that works with many different places (or operating systems), it can run on all of them, just like your toy car can follow the same instructions whether you’re at home or in the park!
